why: Visitors spend only a few seconds deciding whether to keep reading. If the top does not say what the project is and whether anyone still maintains it, they close the tab.
question: What is this, and is it still maintained?
questionNote: Right at the very top of the README
who: Required for all four project types
whoNote: Even for a personal practice project

parts.heading: # Project Name
parts.text: Put it on the first line as the only top-level heading in the file.
parts.emphasis: Put no badges, images, or notes above the title.

parts.heading: One-line description
parts.text: Right below the title, say in one plain sentence what the project does and who it is for, within 120 characters.
parts.emphasis: Do not format it as a > quote or turn it into a long backstory.

parts.heading: Project status
parts.text: On the next line, write "Status: maintained", "Status: completed", or "Status: practice project" so readers know whether it is still updated.

lines.text: [[>]] [[Morning lines are long, so we built this system with]]
[[> Vue 3 and Vite to digitize local breakfast shops.]]

notes.title: Badges above the title
notes.text: Start with the title; star counts show no quality.

notes.title: Description written as quote
notes.text: A leading > looks like a quote; use plain text.

notes.title: Description is too long
notes.text: Keep what it does and for whom; move details down.

notes.title: Missing project status
notes.text: Add a status line so readers know it is maintained.

lines: A web app to order on your phone and pick up in store.

tip.title: Reuse this one sentence in three places
paragraphs: Once you have this sentence, paste the same line into the GitHub repository's About box and the description field in package.json.
Keeping all three identical means people see the same summary whether they find you through search, a package registry, or the repository itself.

types.web-app: Say who uses it and when, rather than "A website built with Vue."
types.course-example: Name the course and lesson in the description or status so students know they opened the right repository.
types.portfolio: Interviewers often open a dozen tabs at once; make the first sentence clear about the problem your project solves.
types.backend-api: State what data this API serves and which frontend or service calls it.
